posts.author: DJ Mathson
posts.content_md: I am wondering if I could use a laboratory shaker to agitate the developing trays. What kind of shaker do you think would work best? One that shakes in one direction, in a circular motion or by rocking the tray? Could any or all of these techniques give bad results with uneven development? I suppose it would be best to have random movement, but that is diffult to achieve with the shakers that I know of.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
I tried shaking my developer in a circular motion for a while. I was doing coherence length tests by making 2.5" x 2.5" exposures on film. I would then change the temperature of the diode and try again. I did not have wler's cool tools! I was trying to make similar map but one hologram at a time.

I found when I swirled the tray, it was round, I would get density on the edges before the middle. This is backwards of the exposure energy so I abandoned it and started rocking the developer in a back and forth motion. Waves.

I could then pump the alcohol through heating elements to keep the liquid at a stable temperature. I don't know if this would work for silver processing because of possible reaction with the metal heating element.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: I am going to have to say that I believe you must be careful with the type of agitation as some may actually cause contructive and destructive zones in which you may see uneven development or fringes of development if you will. Just a thought.
